content.value_statement: Cloud migrations are difficult when services, runtimes, and identity models differ. This skill structures Azure assessment and migration guidance for serverless workloads.
actual_capabilities: Creates a phased assessment workflow before code migration starts.
Maps AWS Lambda services and triggers to Azure Functions equivalents.
Provides runtime-specific Azure Functions patterns for six languages.
Guides managed identity configuration for Azure app settings.
Keeps migrated output in a separate workspace folder.
Prepares handoff context for Azure infrastructure and deployment steps.
limitations: The strongest coverage is for AWS Lambda to Azure Functions migrations.
It does not deploy infrastructure directly after code migration.
It requires source files and user review for accurate assessment.
Production readiness still requires tests, validation, and security review.

use_cases.title: Assess a Lambda Migration
use_cases.description: Review functions, triggers, dependencies, service mappings, and readiness before committing to Azure migration work.

use_cases.title: Convert Serverless Code
use_cases.description: Translate Lambda handlers into Azure Functions patterns for the selected runtime and programming model.

use_cases.title: Plan Azure Platform Requirements
use_cases.description: Identify identity, storage, Event Grid, monitoring, and Bicep requirements for the migrated Functions app.

prompt_templates.title: Start Migration Assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment for a Lambda project
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this AWS Lambda folder for migration to Azure Functions. Identify functions, triggers, dependencies, service mappings, and migration readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Map Services and Triggers
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this serverless workload with Azure Functions. Map each AWS service, trigger, environment setting, and monitoring component to an Azure equivalent.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for these Lambda functions. Include target runtime, Azure Functions binding patterns, dependency changes, and validation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Complex Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan migration for a serverless app using S3 events, DynamoDB, SQS, and CloudWatch. Recommend Azure services, identity, Bicep requirements, and deployment handoff steps.

output_examples.input: Assess a Lambda image-processing app that uses S3 events and Rekognition.
output_examples.output: A readiness report with function inventory, service mapping, trigger mapping, identity recommendations, and migration next steps.

output_examples.input: Convert a Node.js Lambda handler to Azure Functions.
output_examples.output: A migration plan that selects the Azure Functions v4 model, recommends bindings, updates dependencies, and records test tasks.

output_examples.input: Prepare handoff after code migration is complete.
output_examples.output: A status update that summarizes completed migration work and lists infrastructure requirements for the Azure preparation phase.

best_practices: Complete the assessment report before changing source code.
Use managed identity and Azure RBAC instead of connection strings or keys.
Keep migrated files in the separate output folder and preserve the source folder.
anti_patterns: Skipping assessment and converting code without service mapping.
Creating function.json files for JavaScript v4 or Python v2 Functions apps.
Using local auth secrets when managed identity is available.

faq.question: What cloud migrations does this skill support best?
faq.answer: It is strongest for AWS Lambda to Azure Functions migrations, including serverless triggers and related Azure service mappings.

faq.question: Does it modify the original source folder?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs migrated output to a separate folder at the workspace root.

faq.question: Does it deploy Azure infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It prepares handoff context for Azure infrastructure, validation, and deployment skills after code migration.

faq.question: Which runtimes are covered?
faq.answer: The references include JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C#, Java, and PowerShell Azure Functions patterns.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: The guidance prefers managed identity, Azure RBAC, and app settings over API keys or connection strings.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
